QUESTION: What characterizing property does the Boardman–Vogt tensor product $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ of two operads have in terms of categories of algebras?

ATOM: For operads $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$, the Boardman–Vogt tensor product $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ is an operad with the property that there are equivalences of categories $\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{Q}}(\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}}) \simeq \mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}} \simeq \mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{P}}(\mathrm{Alg}_{\mathbf{Q}})$.
KEY POINTS:
1. Algebras over $\mathbf{P}\otimes\mathbf{Q}$ are equivalent to $\mathbf{Q}$-algebras in the category of $\mathbf{P}$-algebras
2. Equivalently, they are equivalent to $\mathbf{P}$-algebras in the category of $\mathbf{Q}$-algebras, so the order of nesting does not matter

ANSWER TO GRADE:
The category of \((\mathbf P\otimes\mathbf Q)\)-algebras is naturally equivalent to the category of \(\mathbf P\)-algebras in \(\mathbf Q\)-algebras, and equivalently to the category of \(\mathbf Q\)-algebras in \(\mathbf P\)-algebras. In other words, such an algebra has commuting \(\mathbf P\)- and \(\mathbf Q\)-algebra structures.
